kartice.naslov: Separation, isolation, and membrane lipid profiling of selectively vulnerable and resilient neurons
kartice.povzetek_sl: Certain neurons are more susceptible to pathogenic stressors and degenerate, while others remain resilient in neurodegenerative diseases. However, the mechanisms underlying this cell-to-cell heterogeneity in neuronal vulnerability remain unclear, primarily due to challenges in isolating vulnerable and resilient neurons to characterize their properties. In this study, we report the development of a novel cell-labeling method utilizing two cell-impermeable dyes to identify vulnerable and resilient neurons in culture, which are subsequently separated and isolated via fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS). As a proof-of-concept of a mechanistic study, we conducted lipidomic analysis to determine whether the lipid composition of membranes differs between vulnerable and resilient neurons to oxidative stress. This simple but unique method sets the groundwork for investigating the molecular underpinnings of selective neuronal vulnerability, which could inform new diagnostic strategies and therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative diseases.

kartice.povzetek_sl: Transient K+ efflux occurs rapidly following pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP) perception by pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) as part of pattern-triggered immunity (PTI). Electrophysiological analyses indicate that BIK1 inhibits GORK activity in a kinase-dependent manner and that T199 plays an essential role for GORK function. kartice.naslov: A Novel Computational Framework to Investigate the Biomechanics of Burrowing
kartice.povzetek_sl: Head-first burrowing likely imposes strong mechanical demands on the skull of fossorial vertebrates, but how cranial tissues respond to these loads remains obscure. Here, we developed a computational framework integrating the discrete element method (DEM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to investigate cranial biomechanics during burrowing. We used Blanus cinereus, a round-headed amphisbaenian, as a model to establish DEM predictions that were validated and calibrated against in vitro experiments across three substrates and compared with in vivo push forces. DEM-calibrated particle contact forces were then transferred to an anatomically detailed finite element model to quantify cranial loading. The analyses suggested that soft tissues accommodated substantial deformation, while the skull transmitted burrowing loads from the premaxilla towards the occipital region. Cranial sutures further redistributed stresses and strains within the skull. This validated DEM-FEA framework links particle-scale substrate interactions with internal cranial biomechanics and provides a quantitative approach for investigating the mechanics of head-first burrowing across fossorial vertebrates.
